title: PowerToys Run reports a missing Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent dependency

status.label: Likely packaging or deployment dependency failure
status.detail: The public stack trace reaches ETWTrace.Stop and cannot load TraceEvent 3.1.16.0 after an update.

next_action.label: Approve dependency-packaging fix design
next_action.reason: Confirm whether the installed package contains the required TraceEvent assembly before implementing a packaging or defensive telemetry cleanup fix.

judgment.rationale: The issue includes a concrete FileNotFoundException naming the missing assembly and version, making a deployment or assembly-resolution defect more likely than an unexplained Run failure.
evidence: PowerToys Run reports System.IO.FileNotFoundException for Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent, Version=3.1.16.0.
The stack trace fails during Microsoft.PowerToys.Telemetry.ETWTrace.Stop and Dispose.
The report identifies WinGet installation and a post-update launch failure.
Current ETWTrace.cs directly references Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent.Session and disposes the trace session during shutdown.
judgment.recommended_action: Inspect the WinGet-installed package contents and project publish dependency metadata, then ensure the exact TraceEvent dependency is deployed or telemetry shutdown degrades safely when the optional dependency is unavailable.

fix_assessment.rationale: No public fix or linked implementation was identified; the failure maps directly to the telemetry assembly load path.

proposed_fixes.title: Ensure TraceEvent is deployed and telemetry cleanup is resilient
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The updated PowerToys Run installation cannot resolve the Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent assembly required by ETWTrace.Stop.
plan: Verify the TraceEvent package version and private dependency copy settings for PowerToys Run and the installer.
Ensure the required assembly is included in WinGet and self-contained deployment outputs.
Guard optional telemetry cleanup so a missing dependency cannot surface as a launch or shutdown failure.
Add package-content and telemetry disposal regression coverage.
verification: Install the produced WinGet package and confirm PowerToys Run launches without the FileNotFoundException.
Start and stop telemetry recording with the dependency present and absent, confirming cleanup does not crash the process.
Verify the packaged assembly version matches the runtime binding requirement.

confidence.rationale: The missing assembly and exact failing symbol are confirmed, but the public report does not prove whether the root cause is packaging, binding policy, or an incomplete update.

issue_context.summary: A WinGet-updated PowerToys Run installation fails around startup or shutdown because ETW telemetry cannot load Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent 3.1.16.0.
known_information: The issue is open and labeled Issue-Bug and Needs-Triage.
The report supplies PowerToys 0.101.2362.0, WinGet installation, Windows build 26200, and a diagnostic text attachment.
The exception names Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent 3.1.16.0 as missing.
The stack reaches ETWTrace.Stop, Dispose(Boolean), and PowerLauncher.App.Main.
inferences: The update may have left the application with an incomplete or mismatched dependency set.
Telemetry cleanup is likely too tightly coupled to optional TraceEvent availability.
The failure may be specific to the WinGet update/package path rather than all installation methods.
issue_context.analysis: The report contains enough evidence for a focused packaging and cleanup design, but the installed file set is needed to distinguish missing deployment from assembly-binding mismatch.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, labels, attachment link, and current activity.
Reviewed ETWTrace.Start, Stop, Dispose, and the direct TraceEventSession dependency.
No linked public fix or duplicate was identified.

information_gaps.information: Whether Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent.dll is present in the failing WinGet installation and which file version it contains.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes incomplete packaging from runtime binding mismatch.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Inspect the installed PowerToys directory immediately after reproducing and attach a fresh /bugreport.

information_gaps.information: Whether the same build fails after a clean reinstall or only after the update path.
information_gaps.why_needed: This identifies whether stale update contents are required to reproduce the failure.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Compare clean-install and update-in-place results on the same build.

actions.label: Approve TraceEvent deployment and cleanup design
actions.note: Draft only; no upstream action is posted.

comment.body:
Thanks for the report. Please provide:

1. Whether Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent.dll is present in the failing WinGet installation and which file version it contains. Collection: Inspect the installed PowerToys directory immediately after reproducing and attach a fresh /bugreport.
2. Whether the same build fails after a clean reinstall or only after the update path. Collection: Compare clean-install and update-in-place results on the same build.
